environment: all lexical syllables in Green's analysis
attested_analysis: An onset is obligatory; all consonants except placeless nasal /N/ are allowed in onset position.
source_locator: Green 2005 pp.4-5; §1.2; consonant inventory and onset/coda distribution
profile_scope: Green's broad Modern Burmese analysis; source-specific inventory
implementation_consequence: Do not emit vowel-initial IPA from a bare orthographic vowel without an independently supported onset analysis.

attested_analysis: Major syllables may have a simple C or complex C+glide onset; Green's examples include /mj/.
profile_scope: Green's major-syllable analysis; not a complete segmental cluster inventory
implementation_consequence: A general C(G) template does not license every possible consonant+glide pair.

attested_analysis: Complex onsets are excluded from minor syllables; minor syllables have only a simple C onset.
profile_scope: Green's major/minor syllable distinction; do not generalize to major syllables
implementation_consequence: Rejecting C+glide in a minor-syllable analysis is source-scoped; it is not a global Burmese cluster ban.

attested_analysis: Green's analysis permits onset clusters only at foot-initial position; the syllable-initial cluster constraint is ranked differently at foot edge.
profile_scope: Prosodic analysis in Green 2005; foot structure is not available from orthography alone
implementation_consequence: Do not enforce foot-initial legality in the grapheme parser; prosodic parse and lexical context would be required.

attested_analysis: When a major syllable with a complex onset becomes minor in a reducing compound, the second onset consonant is lost in Green's examples.
profile_scope: Reduction in the compounds discussed by Green; not a general orthographic rewrite rule
implementation_consequence: Do not rewrite source spelling or generate a reduced form without lexical/morphological evidence.

attested_analysis: Green gives /mj/ in mjè: 'earth' and mjɛʔ 'eye'; this attests a glide-bearing onset in his broad analysis, not a Unicode medial-to-IPA mapping.
profile_scope: Examples cited by Green; exact mapping to modern orthographic medial signs is not established by this row
implementation_consequence: Preserve /mj/ as a source-attested analysis; do not infer that every written YA/RA sequence is /mj/.

attested_analysis: Ishida describes YA/RA as normally /j/ and documents palatalized outcomes after velar stops (and a selected velar nasal example); this is not a universal /j/ segment rule.
source_locator: Ishida 2026, Onsets > Medial YA and RA; examples ပျော် ပြည် ကျောင်း ကြက် ဂျပန် ငြ
profile_scope: Modern Burmese orthography notes; descriptive reference, not an acoustic corpus
implementation_consequence: Keep onset-conditioned palatalization distinct from simple C+/j/ concatenation; do not infer a complete legal cluster inventory.

attested_analysis: Ishida describes WA as /w/ in glide contexts but notes that it can represent /ʊ/ in vowel/rime environments.
source_locator: Ishida 2026, Medial WA and plainV; example နွား
profile_scope: Modern Burmese orthography notes; context-sensitive descriptive account
implementation_consequence: Do not map every U+103D to an onset /w/.

attested_analysis: Ishida describes aspiration/devoicing effects and selected /ʃ/ outcomes; U+103E is not a universal independent /h/ segment.
source_locator: Ishida 2026, Medial HA; examples မှာ ရှိတယ် လျှ မြွှ
profile_scope: Modern Burmese orthography notes; not a full onset-by-onset acoustic analysis
implementation_consequence: Do not append /h/ mechanically; retain source sequence and withhold unsupported realization.

attested_analysis: The listed multi-medial forms establish orthographic combinations only; they do not establish a concatenation of independent phonological segments.
source_locator: Hlaing 2014 Table 5 p.26; Unicode/MLC combination inventory
profile_scope: Myanmar orthographic syllabification; not a phonological legality or IPA inventory
implementation_consequence: Use combinations for structural parsing and fixtures only; no automatic segment concatenation.

attested_analysis: The STEDT Written Burmese analysis treats /-y-/ and /-r-/ as initial-cluster components while /-w-/ belongs to the rhyme; this is source-specific historical analysis.
profile_scope: Written Burmese inventory; not a direct mapping to modern Yangon Unicode spellings
implementation_consequence: Keep historical written-Burmese segmentation separate from modern spoken-Burmese medial realization.

attested_analysis: Burling and Roop describe source-specific distributions; Roop restricts /r/ to borrowings in the cited account.
source_locator: STEDT Monograph 3 pp.63-66; Burling 1967 pp.13-15; Roop 1972 pp.xi-xiii
profile_scope: Historical Rangoon inventories; not a current standard Yangon runtime rule
implementation_consequence: Do not merge historical dialectal inventories into one modern standard medial rule.

attested_analysis: Only placeless glottal /ʔ/ and placeless nasal /N/ are allowed as codas; /N/ is realized through preceding-vowel nasalization in Green's account.
source_locator: Green 2005 pp.4-5; §1.2; coda inventory and place realization
profile_scope: Green's coda analysis; phonemic /N/ is not automatically surface [ɴ]
implementation_consequence: Keep orthographic ASAT, phonemic coda, nasalization and surface place realization as separate typed fields.
